chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī Maryam, who said:

Jaʿfar عليه السلام narrated to us, saying: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام used to say: “If a dog dies in the well, it is drawn out.” And Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “If it falls into it and is then taken out of it alive, seven buckets are drawn from it.”

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which water is drawn and whose purity is being discussed
key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: the dog whose falling into the well affects the ruling of the water
key_terms.حَيًّا: alive; indicating that the dog was removed without dying in the well
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets; the specified amount of water to be drawn out in this case
key_terms.مَاتَ: died; indicating the case in which the dog dies inside the well
key_terms.نُزِحَتْ: it is drawn out; referring to drawing out the well water
key_terms.وَقَعَ: fell; indicating the dog’s falling into the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dog falls into a well or dies in it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding well water when a dog falls into it. If the dog dies in the well, the water is to be drawn out, and if it falls in but is removed alive, seven buckets are to be drawn from the well.
